name: next-dev-loop
works_with: Coding agents that load skills. The Next.js repo ships it as a Claude Code plugin
short: Has your agent check that a Next.js change works in the running app, using Next.js's own endpoint and a real browser.
what: An official Next.js skill for the edit and verify loop during `next dev`. After a change, your agent checks two views of the running app: the `/_next/mcp` endpoint, which knows routes, server logs, errors and compile issues, and the agent-browser CLI, which drives a real Chrome and can inspect the DOM, console, network and React components. The two views cross-check each other.
who: Next.js developers on recent versions who let a coding agent edit their app. The requirements are strict: the skill tells your agent to stop if Next.js is older than 16.3, if you use webpack instead of Turbopack, or if agent-browser is too old.

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: The Next.js repo ships a Claude Code plugin marketplace called `nextjs`, with one plugin, also called `nextjs`, that holds this skill and the other official Next.js skills. The files we read don't give a copy-paste install command.

steps.title: Install or upgrade agent-browser
steps.text: The skill expects the CLI on your PATH.

steps.title: Start your dev server
steps.text: Run `next dev` as usual. If it isn't on port 3000, the skill has your agent set `NEXT_MCP_URL` to your port.

try.label: A first prompt
try.where: Your coding agent, with next dev running
try.text: Make a small change to a page, then ask your agent to verify it works in the running app.

watch: agent-browser can save cookies and local storage between sessions so you stay logged in. The skill may pause and open a visible browser for you to log in.
Don't move or delete the `.next` folder while the dev server runs. The skill says that disconnects the server and throws away its caches.
The skill refuses to fall back to weaker checks. If your versions are too old, it stops and tells you to upgrade.
